title: Kinetic relaxation, diffusive scaling and entropy dissipation

items.title: Two-velocity periodic diffusive-scaling model
items.statement:
Fix a period $L>0$ metres and let $\mathbb T_L:=\mathbb R/(L\mathbb Z)$. A smooth periodic function on $\mathbb T_L$ means an $L$-periodic $C^\infty$ function on $\mathbb R$. For a periodic measurable function $g$ with $\int_0^L |g(x)|^2\,dx<\infty$, use the normalized spatial measure $dm_L=dx/L$ on a period and write

$$\|g\|_{2,L}^2:=\frac1L\int_0^L |g(x)|^2\,dx.$$

Elements of $L^2(\mathbb T_L,dm_L;\mathbb C)$ are equivalence classes modulo equality almost everywhere. For $n\in\mathbb Z$, define the wave number $\kappa_n:=2\pi n/L$, character $e_n(x):=\exp(i\kappa_n x)$, and Fourier coefficient $\widehat g(n):=L^{-1}\int_0^L g(x)e^{-i\kappa_nx}\,dx$. These formulas are independent of the chosen representative of $x$ in $\mathbb T_L$.

Let $c>0$ be a speed in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, let $\lambda>0$ be a switching-rate parameter in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, and let $\epsilon>0$ be dimensionless. For smooth real initial data $f_{+,0},f_{-,0}$ on $\mathbb T_L$, the two-velocity periodic model is the linear Cauchy problem below; when these functions represent physical densities, also require $f_{\pm,0}\ge0$.

$$\partial_t f_+^\epsilon+\frac{c}{\epsilon}\partial_x f_+^\epsilon=\frac{\lambda}{\epsilon^2}(f_-^\epsilon-f_+^\epsilon),\qquad \partial_t f_-^\epsilon-\frac{c}{\epsilon}\partial_x f_-^\epsilon=\frac{\lambda}{\epsilon^2}(f_+^\epsilon-f_-^\epsilon),\qquad f_\pm^\epsilon(\cdot,0)=f_{\pm,0}.$$

Here $x\in\mathbb T_L$, $t\ge0$ is measured in seconds, and $f_\pm$ have the units of a linear number density, $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. The speed magnitude is $c/\epsilon$, and from either velocity state the rate of switching to the opposite state is $\lambda/\epsilon^2$. Define the total density $\rho^\epsilon:=f_+^\epsilon+f_-^\epsilon$, the flux $j^\epsilon:=(c/\epsilon)(f_+^\epsilon-f_-^\epsilon)$, and the total mass $M^\epsilon(t):=\int_0^L\rho^\epsilon(x,t)\,dx$.

items.title: Periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann–Grad scaling convention
items.statement:
Fix a dimension $d\ge2$, a period length $L>0$ metres, and an equal particle mass $m>0$ kilograms. The position space is the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^d:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$. For lifts $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$ of points $[x],[y]\in\mathbb T_L^d$, define

$$\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T_L^d}([x],[y]):=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|x-y+Lk|,$$

where $|z|=(\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell^2)^{1/2}$ is the Euclidean norm. For $q_i=[x]$ and $q_j=[y]$, the vectors $x-y+Lk$, $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, are the displacement representatives from $q_j$ to $q_i$. The minimum is attained because $|x-y+Lk|\to\infty$ as $|k|\to\infty$, and its value is independent of the chosen lifts because changing lifts reindexes $k$. For each $N\ge2$ under consideration, let $\delta_N>0$ be the physical sphere diameter in metres and put $a_N:=\delta_N/L$. An admissible configuration $(q_1,\ldots,q_N)$ has pairwise distances $\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T_L^d}(q_i,q_j)>\delta_N$. For a hard-sphere trajectory below, require $\delta_N<L/2$; this restriction holds eventually in the scaling prescription. If two quotient displacement representatives of length $\delta_N$ existed, their difference would be a nonzero vector in $L\mathbb Z^d$, of length at least $L$, but the triangle inequality bounds its length by $2\delta_N<L$; thus the contact normal is unique.

A hard-sphere trajectory, when defined, is specified on one interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior, with time $t\in I$ measured in seconds. For each $i=1,\ldots,N$ its maps are
$$q_i:I\longrightarrow\mathbb T_L^d,\qquad v_i:I\longrightarrow\mathbb R^d,$$
where $v_i$ is measured in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Require $\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T_L^d}(q_i(t),q_j(t))\ge\delta_N$ for every $t\in I$ and $i\ne j$. Every interior time at which equality occurs must be an isolated binary contact as defined below; all pairwise distances are strictly greater than $\delta_N$ at other interior times. The interval may be bounded or unbounded and may include either finite endpoint. Positions are continuous on $I$, and the position and velocity paths are piecewise $C^1$ on its interior away from the isolated binary contacts. On a free-flight interval, $\dot q_i=v_i$ means that any local Euclidean lift of $q_i$ has derivative $v_i$; changing that lift by a constant lattice vector leaves the derivative unchanged. There $\dot v_i=0$. At an interior contact time use both one-sided velocity limits and set $v_i(t_c)=v_i^+$, the outgoing value. A finite endpoint is included only when the corresponding limits from within $I$ exist, and the position and velocity maps take those values there. No collision rule involving a missing side of an endpoint is imposed; a two-sided update there would require an extension of the trajectory through that time. These conventions specify a partial trajectory only and assert no continuation through a collision accumulation. A binary contact of particles $i,j$ at an interior time $t_c\in I^\circ$ means $\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T_L^d}(q_i(t_c),q_j(t_c))=\delta_N$, while no other pair is in contact at $t_c$. Write $v_i^-$ and $v_i^+$ for the one-sided velocity limits at the contact. Let $n$ be the unique unit vector from the centre of $j$ to the centre of $i$ along the shortest quotient displacement. All particles other than $i,j$ retain their velocities at this contact. The equal-mass elastic reflection rule is

$$v_i^+=v_i^- -\bigl((v_i^--v_j^-)\cdot n\bigr)n,\qquad v_j^+=v_j^- +\bigl((v_i^--v_j^-)\cdot n\bigr)n.$$

The Boltzmann–Grad scaling prescription is a sequence, indexed by all sufficiently large integers $N$, with $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to0$, and

$$N a_N^{d-1}=\kappa$$

for a fixed dimensionless $\kappa\in(0,\infty)$. Under this exact relation, $a_N=(\kappa/N)^{1/(d-1)}\to0$, so the trajectory restriction $\delta_N<L/2$ holds for every sufficiently large $N$. The factor $a_N$ is the diameter measured relative to the fixed box length, so the displayed parameter is dimensionless. This is a definition of a finite hard-sphere model and a scaling prescription only; it asserts neither global existence of the hard-sphere flow nor convergence to a Boltzmann equation.

items.title: Well-posedness, positivity and contraction for two-velocity transport
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every $\epsilon>0$, $c,\lambda,L>0$, and smooth real initial pair $(f_{+,0},f_{-,0})$ on $\mathbb T_L$, the periodic system

$$\partial_t f_+^\epsilon+\frac c\epsilon\partial_x f_+^\epsilon=\frac\lambda{\epsilon^2}(f_-^\epsilon-f_+^\epsilon),\qquad \partial_t f_-^\epsilon-\frac c\epsilon\partial_x f_-^\epsilon=\frac\lambda{\epsilon^2}(f_+^\epsilon-f_-^\epsilon),\qquad f_\pm^\epsilon(\cdot,0)=f_{\pm,0}$$

has a unique global smooth solution $(f_+^\epsilon,f_-^\epsilon)$. For a pair $G=(g_+,g_-)$ of square-integrable periodic functions, define $\|G\|_{2,L}^2:=L^{-1}\int_0^L(|g_+|^2+|g_-|^2)\,dx$, and write $F^\epsilon(t):=(f_+^\epsilon(\cdot,t),f_-^\epsilon(\cdot,t))$. Its total mass $M^\epsilon(t)$ is constant. If both initial densities are nonnegative, then both evolved densities are nonnegative. For any two smooth real initial pairs $F_0=(f_{+,0},f_{-,0})$ and $G_0=(g_{+,0},g_{-,0})$, denote their solutions by $F^\epsilon$ and $G^\epsilon$; they satisfy

$$\|F^\epsilon(t)-G^\epsilon(t)\|_{2,L}^2\le \|F_0-G_0\|_{2,L}^2\qquad(t\ge0),$$

In particular, for one solution,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\|F^\epsilon(t)\|_{2,L}^2=-\frac{2\lambda}{\epsilon^2}\|f_+^\epsilon(t)-f_-^\epsilon(t)\|_{2,L}^2\le0.$$

items.title: Periodic two-velocity heat limit for well-prepared data
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix $L>0$, $c,\lambda>0$, and a nonnegative $\rho_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L)$. For each $\epsilon>0$, let $(f_+^\epsilon,f_-^\epsilon)$ solve the two-velocity periodic model with well-prepared initial data $f_+^\epsilon(\cdot,0)=f_-^\epsilon(\cdot,0)=\rho_0/2$, and put $\rho^\epsilon=f_+^\epsilon+f_-^\epsilon$. Let $D:=c^2/(2\lambda)$, which has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$, and define the heat evolution

$$u(t,x):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\widehat{\rho_0}(n)e^{-D\kappa_n^2t}e_n(x).$$

Then $u$ is the smooth periodic solution of $\partial_tu=D\partial_x^2u$ with $u(0)=\rho_0$, and for every finite $T>0$,

$$\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|\rho^\epsilon(t)-u(t)\|_{2,L}=0.$$

This conclusion concerns only the density of the stated linear two-velocity model with well-prepared data.

title: Kinetic relaxation, diffusive scaling and entropy dissipation — Examples

items.title: Distinct kinetic scaling limits
items.statement:
Fix an integer dimension $d\ge2$ and a spatial side length $L>0$ in metres; compare three model families. In the smooth periodic mean-field family, $N\ge2$ equal masses $m>0$ kilograms have positions $q_i\in\mathbb T_L^d$ and canonical momenta $p_i\in\mathbb R^d$ measured in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and move under the Hamiltonian

$$H_N=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{|p_i|^2}{2m}+\frac1N\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W(q_i-q_j),$$

where $W\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d)$ is even and measured in joules. In the periodic hard-sphere family, the dimensionless diameter $a_N=\delta_N/L$ obeys $N a_N^{d-1}=\kappa$ for a fixed $\kappa>0$. In the two-velocity family on $\mathbb T_L$, take $c,\lambda>0$, $\epsilon\downarrow0$, and well-prepared data $f_{+,0}^\epsilon=f_{-,0}^\epsilon=\rho_0/2$ with a nonnegative $\rho_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L)$. Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the two densities have speeds $\pm c/\epsilon$ and switch to the opposite state at rate $\lambda/\epsilon^2$, and their total density has the heat limit with $D=c^2/(2\lambda)$.

These prescriptions use different model variables and interaction rules: respectively a smooth pair force with coefficient $1/N$, hard-core collisions with $N a_N^{d-1}$ fixed, and a two-state linear transport equation with $\epsilon\downarrow0$. This comparison makes no cross-family implication claim and gives no derivation of the nonlinear Boltzmann equation.
